A common yellow flower long favored by the Wardens of Solace for its remarkable endurance-enhancing properties. Vivid in appearance, it has accompanied countless wardens on their journeys across the realm.
A deadly grenade that unleashes a virulent gas.

A journeyman’s axe, the first weapon you ever forged entirely on your own, crafted during the long decades of your apprenticeship. Though imperfect in balance and finish, it remains a trusted weapon, carried with quiet pride, even as you know you will one day have to trade it for something more effective.
A lavish casket found in households of upper class Underdwellers. Usually contains precious jewelry or minerals important to their owner.
A recipe that lists the necessary ingredients for a skin hardening potion.

A red paste traditionally used by the Darkguards, who protect Underdweller settlements against the many dangers of the Underworld. Though its workings remain poorly documented, it is widely believed to grant a decisive edge in moments where survival is measured in seconds.
A relatively rare mineral, even small fragments of it are highly flammable. As such, it is commonly used to aid fire-starting or as a combustion agent in explosives.
A simple but effective helmet that Terul crafted for you.

A simple explosive grenade
Necessary Ingredients:
- Kutracite
- Stoneroot Glue
- Rotvein Powder

A small pile of discarded metal fragments. Though worthless to most craftsmen, the countless jagged edges and broken spikes make it surprisingly useful in the hands of someone with less conventional ideas.
A stained but still sealed document that seems to be addressed towards the Moongate sentry.

A striking red flower of serene beauty, valued far beyond its appearance for its potent healing properties. Rich in a complex mixture of bioactive compounds, it has been cultivated by the Underdwellers for medicinal purposes since their rise to the surface.
Add <PosStat>+10</> Max HP for every flower or shroom  in the inventory
All purpose herb used in tinctures, pastes and alchemy to heal the wounded.

An extremely poisonous and exceptionally rare mushroom found only in deep, lightless caverns. Though unremarkable to the eye, it appears vividly luminous in the infrared spectrum, a trait believed to deter most subterranean life while attracting a single resistant symbiont: the Darkspot Inkling. This tiny spider lives in close association with the fungus, feeding on its outer layer while dispersing its spores through the narrow fissures of the surrounding rock as it moves.
An old bonding ring, gifted to bless the wearer with a long life and quick recoveries shall anything bad happen.

As a reward for their service and loyalty, favored members of Vrög's religious castes are occasionally gifted with ceremonial rings. While some are little more than simple bands of copper, others are said to possess properties that defy ordinary understanding.

Azuremash is seldom used in contemporary Underdweller society. Once prized in medicinal practice for its extraordinary neural potency, its dangerous side effects saw it largely abandoned in favor of safer remedies. Yet certain modern religious sects have revived its use, believing its violent visions grant fleeting sight beyond what they call ‘the Veil’. While many druids of Solace dismiss such spiritual interpretations as misguided superstition, Azuremash’s capacity to heighten neural receptivity has long been acknowledged in certain controlled practices, where it may aid trained practitioners in engaging more precisely with forces others neither perceive nor understand.

Blue Dogbane is named for its peculiar repellent effect on dogs, likely caused by its strong and distinctive scent. While this aroma is perceived as pleasant by most humanoids, it appears to have a profoundly adverse effect on canines. Though commonly cultivated as an ornamental flower, it is also believed to provide a subtle enhancement to cognitive faculties.

Casting Firebolt has a <PosStat>25-65%</> chance to spawn a raging fire conjuration for <PosStat>5s</> when it it hits a living target. The conjuration does <PosStat>10</> fire damage per hit and has a <PosStat>50%</> chance to explode instead of disappear.
Coat your weapon in Poison for a duration of 30s. Enemies hit by a poisoned blade get poisoned for 3s and receive 5 damage every 0.5s. Enemies can have up to 10 Poison stacks
Coat your weapon in Poison for a duration of {Duration}
Common currency which can be used for trading.
Cool and sharp with a crackling bite, a flavour of starlight captured in the night.

Facing a multitude of grueling threats from poisonous insects to giant lizards, and towering armored centipedes, the Darkguards have long stood as a shield against the horrors of the Underworld. The esteem they hold within broader Underdweller society is reflected in the ornate yet functional armor crafted for them by the finest artisans of Kul Dubran.
Forged in the boiling fires of the Ice Peak mountains the rare alloy radiates with fiery strength.
Found almost exclusively in damp areas near small streams and forest ponds, Bog Lichen is known for its subtle invigorating effect and is therefore used in a wide variety of concoctions.
Heavy, but you feel it's worth it.

His current shape might betray his legacy, but this formidable sword was gifted to Kor Maretan by a grateful delegation of Underdweller blacksmiths in recognition of his heroic deeds. Its ornate craftsmanship stands as a testament to the respect and admiration the Underdwellers hold for the rodent’s former identity. He permits you to wield it, though not without clear reluctance... though, in truth, it is not as if you ever needed his permission.
Its intricate craftsmanship whispers tales of an era long past.
Malty,  grainy rich and deep. The taste of this is bittersweet.

Often faced with foes far larger and stronger than themselves, the Darkguards, custodians of the Underdweller settlements and their first line of defense against the dangers of the Underworld, frequently coat their weapons with potent toxins to offset this disadvantage.
Rotvein is a highly toxic rootlike plant that requires no sunlight and is mostly found in very deep underground caves. In dried powder form it is also highly explosive on ignition.

Stoneroot is a rare union of mineral deposit and bacterial growth that spreads through select rock layers in the deep earth, forming vein-like conduits within the stone itself. When broken and ground, it yields a sticky residue known simply as "Stoneroot Glue", long employed by the Underdwellers in construction and craft. Under high heat, however, the substance is known to become violently unstable.

Terul made this dagger for you as one of his first works after bringing the old smithy in Haven back into operation. While simple in function, its ornate detailing cannot quite conceal his artisan past.

The Everkin may well be the single most important lifeform in the history of the Underdwellers. This nourishing, protein-rich fungus thrives even within the lightless depths beneath Solace, where few other edible organisms can endure. For countless generations, its cultivation formed the foundation upon which Underdweller civilization itself was sustained.

The Firecap, named for its fiery crimson hue, has long been prized by the druids of this realm for its potent clotting properties. Though harmful in excess, careful use can swiftly seal wounds and stem bleeding.

The Green Acrimonling derives its name from both its biting stench and its unusually vivid green appearance. The fungus typically thrives on arid, rocky ground in proximity to water sources, where its extensive hydrophoric mycelium grants it a distinct advantage over competing flora and fungi by drawing moisture across considerable distances.

The unusual name of this fungus is believed to stem from its resemblance to the headdresses once worn by the tutors of Kul Dubran's ancient masonry schools. Though these traditions have long faded from memory, the flavorful mushroom still bears their name, preserving a small piece of their history. It is also prized for its use in traditional Underdweller medicine.

This armor was the masterpiece of Kor Fal, the Fourth Warden of Solace. It is said to have taken him nearly five years to complete. The fur and preserved bear’s head, still miraculously intact, are the padded remains of Gren Doran, the ‘Old Sage’, who once dwelled in a large cave near Haven during the long watch of Fal. Though they never came into direct contact, it is said that the Fourth Warden found great peace and inspiration in his occasional sightings of Gren Doran, and so chose to preserve his remains after the great brown bear eventually passed away.
This potent grenate unleashes rapid sharp metalpieces on impact that cut through armor, bone and flesh alike.

This savage looking club has been crafted by one of your predecessors from a Stoneoak shaft, Tarmugon fangs, and two Frosttroll skulls, said to come from the secluded ice caves of the ‘White Shield’, a vast glacier in the central cordillera of Solace.

This striking yellow paste is a potent stimulant. Originally developed for medicinal use, it soon found its way into workshops, mines, and labor crews across the depths, where its ability to ward off fatigue often outweighed concerns about its long-term effects.

Though burdened by a rather unfortunate history as a means of resolving certain domestic grievances, Widowhaulm is nowadays primarily used to control the many pests of the underworld. As such, it can be found in nearly every Underdweller household.
Upon quaffing thereof, the imbiber shall discover that many certainties formerly held with unwavering confidence were, perhaps, arrived at with undue haste.
Using magic of the ancient, this torch uncovers the secrets of the dark.

Usually found on exposed rock surfaces the Rockflower is, biologically speaking, not actually a flower but a lichen that has been named after its decorative appearance even though it can be rather hard to spot.

Whosoever doth partake thereof shall find himself possessed of one further opportunity to pursue those disciplines hitherto denied unto him, albeit by means most obscure and of no discernible natural order.

A dangerous passage leading through the mountain up to Mar Guran.

Carved deep into stone and earth, the waterways have long served as lifelines for the Underdwellers. 

As attention gradually turned toward the upper echelons, 
these ancient systems were repurposed. 

Once carrying fresh water, they now bear the more… 

unpleasant remnants of densely populated depths.

Exhausted from your first expedition, you are about to finally reach Haven, ancient seat and sanctuary of the Druids of Solace.

Your watch began in blood.

What first seemed a distant skirmish now reveals itself for what it truly is...

Slaughter.

Across the island of Solace’s towering peaks, boreal forests, winding deltas, and endless caverns, beauty and horror walk hand in hand.

Monsters. Sickness. Violence.

Dangers above and below.

And then... your Muran Tor.

Your spirit guide.

Nothing like you expected...

The caves were filled with horrors...

Yet as the only path to the remote temple city upon the peaks of Mar Guran, you had no choice but to traverse the seemingly endless caverns and tunnels.

Now you have entered the ancient Haulways, 
carved deep into solid rock by the Underdwellers of old.

Though you are still far beneath the surface, faint rays of sunlight and the touch of fresh wind promise the end of your arduous ascent...

The great dichotomy that once drove a wedge through the flourishing culture of the Underdwellers gave rise to two distinct ways of life.

While one faction remained true to the old enlightened teachings and studied the wonders of the Upper World in quiet fascination, the other underwent a drastic transformation. Religious fanaticism and grand delusion took hold. Ever larger constructions followed, temples reaching toward the sky, slowly claiming the highest peaks as their dominion.

And so it was with Mar Guran, the Father of Stone.

Access to his colossal temple complex is guarded, roughly five hundred vertical meters below the summit, by a gigantic gate known as the Moon Gate.

The arrival of the Sundweller armies left a wide path of devastation. However, the continued presence of enemy forces after all these years also gives rise to hope that the Moon Gate may still stand to this day...

The labyrinthine passages bear witness to centuries of continuous construction.

Many corridors appear to serve no clear purpose, as the relentless pursuit of ever greater heights slowly transformed them into storage vaults, trade routes, and crude sleeping quarters for the legions of stonemasons and laborers required for the grand religious projects.

Yet the craftsmanship remains remarkable. Even after centuries, and despite the destruction of recent years, much of the masonry still stands largely intact...

Before journeying on, you have to prove yourself. Find the portal room underneath Haven.

To reach the Moongate, we must ascend the slopes of Mar Guran, the mountain beneath which the forebears of the Underdwellers first emerged onto the surface after centuries beneath the earth.

Our path leads through the caverns carved by the underground river Koturmak and across the ancient tunnels and settlements that once marked the slow upward ascent of the Underdweller civilization itself.

But these depths have long since fallen silent. The hordes of Vrög now infest the surrounding regions, and far older horrors still linger in the dark below.

Haven, sanctuary of the Watchers of Solace, rests upon a secluded mountain plateau overlooking the northern fjords. Though its ancient walls bear the weight of centuries of hardship and sacrifice, a strange serenity lingers here, as if the spirits of past wardens still stand watch over this place.
